title: Build signed reproducible release artifacts — tamper and wrong-key failure evidence
summary: Negative-path evidence: a signed file that is modified after signing MUST fail GPG verification, and a signature from an unrelated key MUST fail verification against the original key's keyring. Both invariants are asserted by packaging/tests/test_release_signatures.sh gates 4 and 5. The test generates two throwaway Ed25519 GPG keys in isolated GNUPGHOME tempdirs (cleaned on exit), signs a payload with key A, then (a) flips one byte in the payload and confirms GPG verification fails (BAD signature), and (b) signs the same payload with key B and confirms verification against key A's keyring fails (NO_PUBKEY / WRONG key). The wrong-key signature DOES verify in key B's own keyring — a sanity check that the signature itself is well-formed and the failure is specifically a key-mismatch failure, not a malformed-signature false positive.

tamper_evidence.method: sign payload.bin with key A → produce payload.bin.asc → copy payload to payload.tampered.bin → flip byte at offset 10 → gpg --verify payload.bin.asc payload.tampered.bin
tamper_evidence.expected: verification fails (GPG reports BAD signature: the signature hash no longer matches the modified content)

wrong_key_evidence.method: generate unrelated key B in separate GNUPGHOME → sign payload.bin with key B → produce payload.wrong.asc → gpg --verify payload.wrong.asc payload.bin (in key A's keyring)
wrong_key_evidence.expected: verification fails (GPG reports the signature was produced by a key not present in key A's keyring — NO_PUBKEY or key-mismatch)
wrong_key_evidence.actual: verification fails against key A's keyring; verifies against key B's keyring (sanity)
wrong_key_evidence.sanity_check: the wrong-key signature verifies in key B's own keyring, proving the signature is well-formed and the failure is a key-mismatch, not a corrupt signature

no_private_key_evidence.check_1: grep -rEl 'BEGIN.*PRIVATE KEY BLOCK' packaging/ → no matches (no private key blocks committed)
no_private_key_evidence.check_3: test throwaway GNUPGHOMEs are confined to the test tempdir (mktemp -d) and removed by the EXIT trap
no_private_key_evidence.check_4: gpg --armor --export <keyid> produces a public-key block with no 'PRIVATE KEY' markers
no_private_key_evidence.result: PASS — no private key material enters the repo or any release artifact

test_assertions.tamper_fails: PASS — gpg --verify on tampered file exits non-zero
test_assertions.wrong_key_fails_against_original_keyring: PASS — gpg --verify of wrong-key .asc in key A keyring exits non-zero
test_assertions.wrong_key_verifies_in_own_keyring: PASS — sanity: the wrong-key .asc verifies in key B keyring (signature is well-formed)
test_assertions.no_private_key_in_packaging: PASS — grep for private key blocks under packaging/ returns empty
test_assertions.script_never_handles_secrets: PASS — sign-packages.sh has no generate/export/import secret-key operations
test_assertions.keyring_confined_to_tempdir: PASS — both test GNUPGHOMEs are under $tmp (mktemp -d), removed on EXIT
test_assertions.public_export_clean: PASS — gpg --export output contains no PRIVATE KEY markers
